also: take it with a pinch of salt
take with a grain of salt

terms.comment: We have found no ancient source for it in Lewis & Short or the loci collections.

The phrase is modern Latin, though built on Pliny, who has a remedy taken additō salis grānō (NH 23.149, Lewis & Short s.v. grānum), with a grain of salt added; we have found no classical instance of it in the figurative sense.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
